characters.name: The Mystic Knights as a Group
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: By the Power of Grayskull!: Each knight has a unique invocation for summoning his/her armor."Fire Within Me!" (Rohan)"Earth Beneath Me!" (Angus)"Air Above Me!" (Deirdre)"Water Around Me!" (Ivar)"Forest Before Me!" (Garrett) "Fire Within Me!" (Rohan) "Earth Beneath Me!" (Angus) "Air Above Me!" (Deirdre) "Water Around Me!" (Ivar)

characters.name: Rohan
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: An orphan raised as Cathbad's apprentice before learning he was the long-awaitedChosen OneDraganta, making him the leader by default. He is the only one who can control Pyre, the Dragon of Dare, whom he summons with the Dragon's Breath Dagger. Rohan revealed in one episode his heart's desire is to know who and where his real family is.Be Careful What You Wish For... Mystic Weapon:The Sword of Kells, a sword that shoots flames Arbitrary Skepticism: In the "Night of the Spirits" episode, he and Deirdre both wave off the idea of spirits existing, which seems rather out of place in a world of elves, fairies, dragons, and druids who can perform actual magic. Betty and Veronica:Zigzaggedwith Garrett. For Deirdre's Archie, he's the peasant Betty to Garrett's princely Veronica on one hand, yet his destiny as a fabled warrior who's supposed to bring peace to Kells "for a hundred lifetimes" might make him the Veronica to Garrett's mere mortal Betty on the other.Whatever the case may be, the penultimate episode reveals that Deirdre is in love with him.He's also the Archie for Aideen's Betty (unwaveringly sweet and helpful but tiny fairy) and Deirdre's Veronica (a benevolent yet feisty and initially haughty princess). Zigzaggedwith Garrett. For Deirdre's Archie, he's the peasant Betty to Garrett's princely Veronica on one hand, yet his destiny as a fabled warrior who's supposed to bring peace to Kells "for a hundred lifetimes" might make him the Veronica to Garrett's mere mortal Betty on the other.Whatever the case may be, the penultimate episode reveals that Deirdre is in love with him.

characters.name: Angus
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: Rohan's best friend and roommate. The two grew up on the streets together, and Angus was — and still is — the troublemaker. Rohan trusts him unquestionably (the power of their friendshipwas once enough to free Rohan from a spell), despite his reputation asThe Tricksterand pickpocket. His skills in that area frequently come in handy. Mystic Weapon:Terra Mace, a mace that shoots large boulders and creates earthquakes Achilles in His Tent: The episode "Friends for Life" revolves around Angus's jealousy of all the praise Rohan (or Draganta) gets from the people of Kells for defending their village from Temra attacks, and leaves the team afterwards when the two friends fall out over it. When Rohan gets kidnapped by Tyrune, Maeve's three-headed dragon, he returns to save the day and the two make up afterwards. Blatant Lies: To viewers at least. Near the end of "Legend of the Ancient Scroll", after he and Rohan first encounter, get attacked by, and subdue Ivar, prompting him to realize that neither one of them is the thief who stole his royal family's sacred chalice and apologize for attacking them, Angus lies to Ivar that he knows the thief who stole said chalice and that he and Rohan will help Ivar recover it if he helps them save Kells. Viewers by this point clearly know that (one) Angus and Rohan are just now hearing about such an item and (two) that Angus, being the thief that he is, would've tried to steal such an item forhimselfhad he known about it. Butt-Monkey: If someone is going to suffer a comedic pratfall or some other misfortune, odds are it's going to be Angus.

characters.name: Deirdre
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: TheRebellious Princessof Kells, who finds herself a habitual blackmail tool. In the finale, it took all of one minute for Maeve to grab her and the knights to sulkily abandon their weapons as if it had become routine, which it had. Fortunately,no one in her world seemed to notice, any more than they were bothered by her tendency to pull rank whenever she wanted to get her way. ("That's a royal command.") Mystic Weapon:Whirlwind Crossbow, a crossbow that shoots strong blasts of air Arbitrary Skepticism: In the "Night of the Spirits" episode, she and Rohan both wave off the idea of spirits existing, which seems rather out of place in a world of elves, fairies, dragons, and druids who can perform actual magic. Arranged Marriage: In "Garrett and the Princess", she finds out that she's in this type of engagement with the aforementioned prince, and is unsurprisingly not thrilled about it. Blow You Away: As the Mystic Knight of Air, she summons her armor by saying "Air Above Me!". When wielding her Whirlwind Crossbow, she can shoot concentrated blasts of swirling air energy from it.

characters.name: Ivar
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: A prince who was passing through Kells on the hunt for a thief who stole a priceless chalice from his kingdom. He eventually learned that very chalice was located in Maeve's throne room, since it was Mider's portal between Earth and the Dark Fairy Realm. His dedication to retrieving the chalice almost matched his uncanny ability to track anything and everything. Mystic Weapon:Barbed Trident, a trident that shoots streams of blue electricity. Blue Is Calm: Downplayed. Ivar may have hisHot-Bloodedmoments here and there, but otherwise, he's very much the calmest and most levelheaded member of the team like his element and signature color suggest. Blue Is Heroic: He's a nobleWarrior Princewho wears blue, both when wearing his mystic armor and his civilian clothes outside of it. By the Power of Grayskull!: He summons his mystic armor with invocation of "Water Around Me!".

characters.name: Garrett
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: ASixth Rangerwho came to Kells to carry out his betrothal to Deirdre, who instantly shot him down due to his initial severe superiority complex. After a period of fighting the team after beingBrainwashedby Maeve, Cathbad realized he was destined to be the fifth Mystic Knight. Deirdre firmly refused to go through with the marriage, but she tolerated him as a teammate, even giving him a kiss good-bye when he left almost as quickly as he came to escort a stranded princess home. Mystic Weapon:Twin Timber Axes, which are supposedly "sharp enough to slice a stone in half," but were usually used to shoot energy blasts. Arrogant Kung-Fu Guy: He's a great fighter but incredibly arrogant and self-absorbed as Deidre points out in his first appearance. HeTook a Level in Kindnessbut the ego is still there. Betty and Veronica: The Veronica to Rohan's Betty for Deirdre's Archie.The penultimate episode reveals that Deirdre is in love with Rohan though. Brainwashed and Crazy: After declining Maeve's request/offer to be the commanding officer to her soldiers ("The Traitor of Kells"), he gets spellbound into agreeing by the magic of her scepter.

characters.name: King Conchobar
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The ruler of Kells and father of Deirdre. Badass in Distress:Near the start of "Queen Deirdre", he falls ill after receiving a seashell as a supposed "tribute" from Kells's allies "from across the sea", due to the seashell containing a dark spell that hits him as he examines it. Obviously a tactic by Maeve.While waiting for Deirdre, Angus, Ivar and Garrett to get back to the hut they're all hiding in "Banished", King Conchobar and Cathbad are eventually found and attacked by Temra soldiers. While he bravely fights back against a few of them, he and Cathbad are eventually outnumbered, tied up, and held hostage by Torc as a means to make the four aforementioned Mystic Knights surrender. Near the start of "Queen Deirdre", he falls ill after receiving a seashell as a supposed "tribute" from Kells's allies "from across the sea", due to the seashell containing a dark spell that hits him as he examines it. Obviously a tactic by Maeve. While waiting for Deirdre, Angus, Ivar and Garrett to get back to the hut they're all hiding in "Banished", King Conchobar and Cathbad are eventually found and attacked by Temra soldiers. While he bravely fights back against a few of them, he and Cathbad are eventually outnumbered, tied up, and held hostage by Torc as a means to make the four aforementioned Mystic Knights surrender. Excellent Judge of Character: Early in the latter half of "Legend of the Ancient Scroll", the king gently shoots down Deirdre's request to accompany Rohan on his search for the warrior Draganta, a refusal she seemingly accepts without question before leaving the throne room. However, clearly knowing how headstrong and determined his daughter is, Conchobar quickly orders one of his guards to keep watch over Deirdre, noting that her acceptance of his refusal was too easy. Sure enough, she manages to sneak out of the castle.

characters.name: Cathbad
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: Badass in Distress: While waiting for Deirdre, Angus, Ivar and Garrett to get back to the hut they're all hiding in "Banished", King Conchobar and Cathbad are eventually found and attacked by Temra soldiers. Despite the king's best efforts to fight back against a few of them, they're both eventually outnumbered, tied up, and held hostage by Torc as a means to make the four aforementioned Mystic Knights surrender. Character Narrator: Later on in the series, Cathbad began to narrate exposition they didn't have to film, or the beginning of episodes to catch people up to the story. Detect Evil: In "The Barrow of Balin", when Rohan leads the titular hero (who's under Maeve's control unbeknownst to him) to King Conchobar's throne room to meet Cathbad, Cathbad regretfully informs everyone that he can sense Maeve's dark magic possessing Balin, and that the spellbound hero has come to take him away. Dispel Magic: Near the beginning of "The Queen Mother", right when Cathbad, the Mystic Knights, and King Conchobar are about to eat after aRousing Speechdelivered by Rohan to Kells soldiers, he immediately senses an enchantment spell that Maeve casts on Rohan from the safety of her castle. When the spell causes Rohan to attempt to leave the castle, andattackthe other three Mystic Knights as they try to stop him, Cathbad casts a blue-colored energy spell to remove the spell and block it. Druid: Of course. He's the official court Druid of Kells.

characters.name: Fin Varra
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The fairy king of Tir Na Nog who gave the Mystic Knights their weapons and armor. They frequently came to him for help but more often than not heardFigure It Out Yourself, in riddle form. Aloof Ally: At first, so much so in fact that he made the knights take aTest Of Characterbefore he agreed to help. The Fair Folk: The king .

characters.name: Aideen
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: A fairy who followed the Knights around, serving as a messenger and spy. She had a crush on Rohan that occasionally caused her to do foolish things, like having Maeve turn her human or accidentally turning Deirdre to stone. Expy: Aideen is very similar toDisney'sTinker Bell, being a diminutive winged fairy helper to the good guys who has a bit of an attitude, a crush on the main hero (Peter/Rohan) and jealousy towards the heroine (Wendy/Deirdre). Although Aideen speaks, whereas Tinker Bell made a bell-like sound. Fairy Companion: She's this to the Knights, though she shows shades of wishing to be a straighforwardAction Girlrather than aSide Kick. Interspecies Romance: She's a fairy who has a one-sided crush on Rohan, a human.

characters.name: Pyre
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: A red dragon who aids the knights in battle when they summon him with their daggers. Sealed Good in a Can: The spell used to free Tyrune transferred the chains to Pyre and left him trapped in his cave for a bit. Undying Loyalty: To Rohan. This becomes a problem in one episode when Rohan is abducted by Tyrune, and Angus needs to convince Pyre to listen to him instead.

characters.name: Maeve
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: Maeve is the queen of Temra. She believes that being the ruler of Kells is her birthright, so she recruits the help of the dark fairy Mider. Big Bad: Of the show in general.However, she was only supposed to play this role for first season. Big Bad Duumvirate: She works alongside Mider so that both can conquer Kells and Tir Na Nog simultaneously, an arrangement where she tends to flip flop between kissing the dark fairy's ass and working up the nerve to bite back at him at certain times.Following her defeat near the end of "Banished", Mider very quickly jumps ship by striking up a team-up with Nemain afterwards. Birthmark of Destiny:Revealing she has the very same Mark of Destiny on her arm in "The Queen Mother" is how she proves that she is Rohan's mother. Catchphrase: More than once, she claims that her reasoning for wanting to conquer Kells is because, let her tell it, it's her "birthright".

characters.name: Torc
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: Queen Maeve's right-hand man.Before the series started, he was acting asThe Molefor Maeve in king Conchobar's court before a young Rohan and Angus uncovered his treachery. He was revealed to be the one who stole Ivar's chalice. Animal Theme Naming: In addition to being a type of Celtic necklas, his name "Torc" can mean "wild boar." Though ironically he has a ram-themed helmet instead. Arch-Enemy:To Ivar for stealing his chalice. As Long as It Sounds Foreign: "Torc" is not an actual name in Irish myth or history. In reality, a torc is a type of necklace. It also the Irish word for "boar." Chekhov's Gunman: He established asThe Dragonright away, but it takes a little bit to learn thathe was the one who stole Ivar's chalice, making him responsible for both Ivar being in Kells and Mider using the chalice to enter the world.

characters.name: Mider
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: A dark fairy who wishes to take over the fairy kingdom of Tir Na Nog. To reach that goal, he allies with Queen Maeve and grants her the magical power to create monsters. Bad Boss: Whenever he manages to take charge. Big Bad Duumvirate: He spendsmost ofthe entire series working alongside Maeve so that both can conquer Tir Na Nog and Kells simultaneously, an arrangement that's hardly harmonious or pleasant between.Following Maeve's defeat near the end of "Banished", he very quickly strikes up a team-up with Nemain afterwards. Deal with the Devil:When Maeve begs for him to grant her access to much stronger magic near the beginning of "Legend of the Ancient Scroll", he gives her a rune stone, situated between the horns of her Ram Staff. When Maeve asks him what his price is, he cryptically tells her that he'll collect his payment... in time.Much later on, in "The Queen Mother", he initially refuses Maeve's request to use his magic to cast a stronger mind control spell on Rohan after hers was dispelled by Cathbad,untilshe offers to be his slave if he helps her and she still fails to bring down Kells before the next full moon. When Maeve begs for him to grant her access to much stronger magic near the beginning of "Legend of the Ancient Scroll", he gives her a rune stone, situated between the horns of her Ram Staff. When Maeve asks him what his price is, he cryptically tells her that he'll collect his payment... in time.

characters.name: Nemain
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: A sorceress and Maeve's former teacher, she was the original queen of Temra before Maeve usurped her throne and empire. Animal Motifs: Crows. She makes her first appearance in "The Warrior of Temra" by reverting back to her human form after having morphed into a crow prior to Maeve meeting with her. Additionally, her eyebrows vaguely resemble crow wings in shape, and whenever she teleports away, she leaves behind both a purple-colored energy outline of a crow and the random sound of a crow cawing in her wake. Additionally, near the beginning of "Lugad's Challenge", when she teleports from Maeve's throne room after reminding her of, and doubling down on, her assertion that Lugad isn't ready to fight on behalf of Temra, Maeve calls her a "piece of carrion" to Lugad as she tells the latter not to listen to her. Animorphism: Her shapeshifting allows her to take on animal forms as well as other human forms, as is shown by her first appearance, where she's in the form of a crow before reverting back to her actual human form. Big Bad Duumvirate:In the final moments of the series, she teams up with Mider, setting them up as the main villains for a potential second season that never materialized. Cassandra Truth: Nemain tells Maeve not once buttwicethatLugad isn't ready to fight on behalf of Temra, making it clear that despite her best efforts to feed and enhance his half-demon side, his half-human side, where love, kindness and compassion clearly reside, still remains, and that it'll prove to be his weakness (at least from an evil standpoint) in the long run. Sure enough, she's proven right over the course of the next seven episodes near the end of the series, as Lugad eventually switches sides, due to finding out that he and Rohan are brothers, receiving kindness from Deirdre, and realizing that Maeve, despite being his and Rohan'smother, never cared for him in any capacity beyond his capabilities as a warrior.

characters.name: Lugad
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The warrior of Temra and a half-demon, he was raised by Nemain and brought in by Maeve in a last-ditch attempt to crush Kells. Always Someone Better: To Torc, being substantially stronger and more effective, though significantly less intelligent. Amazing Technicolour Population: He’s yellow, as a result of being half-demon, making him resemble Frankenstein’s Monster. Barbaric Battleaxe: Fitting his characterization as a supernaturally strong brute, Lugad wields an axe (one that can shoot small bolts at that) in battle. Because You Were Nice to Me: He takes a liking to Deirdre after she tends to his wounded hand after he crushes a rock in a fit of rage with it in "The Mark of Destiny".

characters.name: The Sentinels as a Group
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: Back from the Dead: All appeared destroyed at the end of their initial appearances yet were resurrected by Mider and sent after the Knights again. Badass Cape: All four wear long black capes as part of their outfit. The Brute: They're a Brute squad of expendable but powerful muscle, sent out to harass the protagonists when Maeve and Torc are otherwise busy. Evil Wears Black: All of them wear black, with or without another accent colour. Obviously Evil: All four are blatantly the bad guys, what with their spiked dark armours and ominous names.

characters.name: The Ice Lord of Temra
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The guardian of Rohan's armour, the Ice Lord is a skeletal figure wrapped in purple armour. An Ice Person: Highly resistant to cold, he could also lower the temperatures of his sword, freezing those he touched. Disney Villain Death: His initial defeat leaves him plummeting off a cliff after Rohan melts the ice bridge they are fighting. Evil Counterpart: To Rohan, as a swordsman wielding the opposing element to his own. Grim Up North: The Mountains of the North, where he hides out, certainly evoke this.

characters.name: The Lightning Bat of Temra
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The guardian of Dierdre's armour, the Lightning Bat comes armed with a magical boomerang and grating voice. Bat People: A monster bat in knight form to be exact. Evil Counterpart: To Dierdre, as a sky-associated warrior for the other side. Flashy Teleportation: He first appears before Deirdre by materializing from a bolt of lightning. Non-Indicative Name: Despite lightning being given as his attribute, he doesn't have any lightning attacks in his repertoire.

characters.name: The Sea Serpent of Temra
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The guardian of Ivar's armour, the Sea Serpent was a cackling sadist who held a grudge even better than the other Sentinels. Evil Counterpart: Like Ivar he's associated with water, and he has the same ability to obsess over defeats. It's Personal: None of the Sentinels took their first defeat well, but the Sea Serpent seems to have taken his the most personally, returning to harass Ivar as both a member of the Sentinels and independently. Lightning Lash: His primary weapon was his "Serpent's Tongue Whip" which emitted electrical shocks to those it touched. Psycho Electro: Despite his name, his primary power was not based around water but electricity and he was one of the eviler members of the cast.

characters.name: The Rock Wolf of Temra
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The guardian of Angus's armour, the Rock Wolf was stupid, brutish, and completely uninterested in the world around him. Dumb Muscle: None of the four were geniuses but the Rock Wolf was easily the dumbest. Evil Counterpart: To Angus, being associated with stone, none-too-bright, and relentlessly lazy. Eye Beams: Could fire rays of energy from his eyes. Lazy Bum: When Angus first showed up the Rock Wolf didn't even want to fight him and tried to just bluster him into going away. When Angus pressed the issue, the Rock Wolf settled for driving him off, then promptly retreating to his cave.

characters.name: Kallach
characters.media_title: Mystic Knights of Tir Na Nog
characters.description: The guest antagonist of the episode "The Dark Rider", Kallach is a long-dead king and warrior wizard whose spirit has been summoned from the underworld by Maeve and Mider by accident. He seeks to create a new army for himself after losing his original one to King Conchobar's ancestors. Antagonist Title: He's clearly the "dark rider" being referred to in his episode. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: When granted an audience with King Conchobar, with the Mystic Knights and Cathbad present of course, Kallach initially speaks with a pleasant demeanor, even apologizing to the king for meeting with him on short notice. However, that initial air of good will quickly goes away when he explains who he is and what his intentions are. He promptly attacks King Conchobar and company shortly afterwards. Celestial Deadline: He informs Maeve that he has to complete his goals while making sure to return to the underworld before sunset, or he'll turn back into a ghost and lose his magic powers. Evil Sorcerer: He's an evil and undead warrior wizard who seeks to rebuild his army by controlling the minds of the mightiest warriors in the current timeline of the show. Maeve wastes no time in pointing him in the direction of the Mystic Knights to achieve that goal.
